mechanism_evidence.contract: SessionRunner owns a slice copy of the global posargs list: runner.posargs is not global_config.posargs; extending one session leaves the global config and sibling sessions untouched; captured at SessionRunner init timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Create two sessions sharing a global config, extend one posargs.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: SessionRunner aliases global_config.posargs; mutating one session pollutes the global config and sibling sessions.

discriminating_observation.description:
from unittest import mock
import nox.sessions, nox.manifest
from nox import _options
cfg = _options.options.namespace(posargs=["--orig"])
runner = nox.sessions.SessionRunner(name="test", signatures=["test"], func=mock.sentinel.func, global_config=cfg, manifest=mock.create_autospec(nox.manifest.Manifest))
print('copy_identity', runner.posargs is not cfg.posargs)
assert runner.posargs is not cfg.posargs
runner.posargs.append("--new")
assert cfg.posargs == ["--orig"]
print('f2_posargs_isolation', True)

triple.is_identity: runner.posargs is not global_config.posargs (slice owns a new list)
triple.shared_mutation_visibility: extending one session leaves the global config untouched

mechanism_evidence.contract: Response owns a copy of caller headers: resp.headers is not the input CIMultiDict; preparing the response never mutates the shared input; captured at the Response(headers=...) call timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Construct web.Response with a shared CIMultiDict and prepare it.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: Response aliases a CIMultiDict input; preparing one response pollutes the caller dict with Content-Length/Date.

discriminating_observation.description:
from multidict import CIMultiDict
from aiohttp import web
h = CIMultiDict({"X-Base": "1"})
r = web.Response(body=b"answer", headers=h)
print('copy_identity', r.headers is not h)
assert r.headers is not h
r.headers["X-New"] = "2"
assert "X-New" not in h
print('f2_headers_isolation', True)

triple.is_identity: resp.headers is not the input headers dict
triple.shared_mutation_visibility: mutating the response leaves the caller dict untouched
